source: MESA International & LNS Research, "Metrics That Matter" survey
methodology: Average OEE across surveyed manufacturers = 71 (used as p50). The top-performing 11% of surveyed manufacturers averaged OEE >=80, used here as an approximate 90th-percentile anchor (the top 11% of a population starts at roughly its 89th percentile boundary, so this is a close but not exact match to a true 90th percentile). Vorne Industries/OEE.com's widely-cited rule-of-thumb figures ("world-class"=85%, "closer to 60%" typical) were deliberately NOT used here, since they are an informal reference page rather than a measured survey.

source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Survey of Occupational Injuries and Illnesses (SOII), 2024
methodology: Total Recordable Cases (TRC) incidence rate per 100 full-time-equivalent workers, Manufacturing sector (NAICS 31-33), 2024 (most recent published year). For reference, the DART (days-away/restricted/transferred) sub-rate is 1.7, and the all-private-industry TRC average is 2.3 (manufacturing runs above the general private-sector average); neither is used as a second percentile point here since both describe a different case-type or a different population, not a percentile of manufacturing companies specifically. Single point only — below this platform's 2-point minimum for peer-headroom scoring until a second point is sourced.
